D023-D009_h024.question:
It’s been going on for a few years now, but it’s gotten worse this past year. I have these spells where I feel “up” for days at a time. I don’t sleep much, maybe three or four hours, but I don’t feel tired. I’m talking nonstop to the other ladies, getting into everybody’s business, making all these plans about starting activities here, like I’m in charge of the place. The staff tell me I’m more argumentative and wound up. My thoughts feel like they’re racing, jumping from one thing to another, and I feel unusually confident, like I can do everything myself even though I’m 82 and use a walker.

During those times, I also eat a lot. I’ll sit in my room with snacks I’ve hidden and just keep eating and eating in one sitting—far more than the others would eat—until my stomach hurts and I feel sick. I try to do it when my roommate is at bingo because I’m ashamed of how much I’m putting away. After these “high” periods, I usually crash into feeling low and empty for weeks.
D023-D009_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D023-D009_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling with these episodes for a little over a year now. It tends to happen in these “up” phases I get every few weeks. I’ll be buzzing with energy, sleeping maybe three or four hours and still showing up at school at 6 a.m., talking a mile a minute, starting new programs on a whim, feeling like I can handle everything at once. My staff will tell me to slow down, but I feel almost invincible in those times.

During those stretches, I’ll come home late, still wired, and just start eating. I can go through half a pizza, a carton of ice cream, bags of chips in maybe an hour, way more than what my family eats for dinner. I keep going until my stomach hurts and I feel physically stuffed. I’m so ashamed of it that I wait until my husband and kids are asleep, or I’ll sit in the car in the driveway and eat there so no one sees. 

After a few days of this, I usually crash into this low, tired state, but the guilt about the eating and how impulsive I get during the “highs” just lingers.
D023-D009_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
